title: Schedule of Payable Items for Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers
content:
This schedule sets, for each instrument of **Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers**, which charges credit value may pay, whether the credit may be combined with other credits or with a miles payment, and what happens to value left over after a redemption smaller than the balance.

## Schedule A — charges payable with credit value

| Instrument | Government taxes and fees | Seat fees and paid upgrades | Checked bag fees | Partner-operated flights sold under a partner's code | Companion fare and taxes of a companion ticket |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crestline Residual Travel Credit | Yes | No | No | No | No |
| Crestline Flight Credit | Yes | No | No | No | No |
| Crestline Trip Credit | Yes | No | No | No | Yes |
| Crestline Service Recovery eCertificate | No | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Crestline Disruption Voucher | No | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Crestline Denied Boarding Voucher | Yes | No | No | No | Yes |

## Schedule B — combination and remaining value

| Instrument | May be combined with other credits on a ticket | May be combined with an award or miles-plus-cash ticket | Value left after a smaller redemption |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crestline Residual Travel Credit | No | No | forfeited |
| Crestline Flight Credit | Yes | No | retained |
| Crestline Trip Credit | Yes | No | retained |
| Crestline Service Recovery eCertificate | Yes | No | retained |
| Crestline Disruption Voucher | Yes | No | retained |
| Crestline Denied Boarding Voucher | Yes | No | retained |

## Notes

1. "Government taxes and fees" means the taxes and fees on a ticket, as distinct from the base fare.
2. "Value left after a smaller redemption" states the treatment of value remaining when a redemption uses less than the balance: *retained* keeps it on the credit, *forfeited* gives it up.
3. No instrument may pay checked bag fees, pay for a partner-operated flight sold under a partner's code, or be combined with an award or miles-plus-cash ticket.

## Hypothetical example

A passenger holds a Crestline Disruption Voucher and a Crestline Trip Credit. According to Schedule A the voucher may pay seat fees but not taxes, and the Trip Credit may pay taxes but not seat fees. According to Schedule B both may be combined with other credits. The holding is an example only.
